text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] SLO breach: streaming endpoint /v1/stream p99=2.31s (>1.5s SLO), p95=0.92s. Observed sustained tail latency and partial streaming stalls. Top symptom: prefix cache hitrate dropped to ~13% after prefix-hash v3 rollout. Error rate +1.8%. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streams/streaming-slo?orgId=1

oncall-joe: ack, looking now. what time did v3 go out?

maria-sre: I'm seeing a correlated spike in KV miss latency and an uptick in cold-kv fetches. p99 kv latency -> 45ms -> 220ms. Might be higher lookups per request.

sam-ml: Confirmed: prefix-hash v3 rollout started at 2026-03-15T11:12:02Z (canary -> 20% -> 100% auto). Change: added namespace salting + new rotation logic. I deployed the canary this morning.

deploy-bot: rollout:prefix-hash:v3 started by sam-ml at 2026-03-15T11:12:02Z. Canary->20%: success. Canary->50%: success. Canary->100%: success. Commit: 9f4b2d3

oncall-joe: ok, suspected culprit. Can we validate prefix hit curves per shard?

maria-sre: running quick aggregation across kv-monitor. Output snippet:
```
shard-03: prefix_requests=14237 prefix_hits=1849 hitrate=13.0%
shard-07: prefix_requests=9871 prefix_hits=1223 hitrate=12.4%
global: total_requests=479012 total_prefix_hits=62452 hitrate=13.0% (was ~91% yesterday)
```

sam-ml: wow that's awful. Did the salt change explode namespace partitioning? Might be an off-by-one in the hash mod.

ops-bot: recent config change: prefix-hash.modulus = 4096 -> 65536 (applied with v3). Also prefetch/shard-allocator mapping updated.

oncall-joe: that modulus jump could break hotkey locality. If dimishing locality, prefetch warms won't target the same shard. That explains the low hit rate and elevated backend load leading to tail stalls.

jess-product: Customer escalation: several large tenants reported streaming stalls and partial transcodes failing. CS ticket #CS-5123. Nate, do we have impact summary?

nate-cs: Customer list: 4x enterprise tenants with heavy streaming traffic saw 10-40% slow responses; 2 tenants reported transient OOM/retry cascading at their side due to repeated partial responses. Severity: P1 -> we already notified their TAMs.

maria-sre: quick mitigation options:
- rollback prefix-hash to v2 (fast path)
- force non-prefetch fallback for streaming route for 15m to reduce cache pressure
- selectively throttle canary traffic to heavy tenants (rate-limit)

oncall-joe: I'm going to attempt rollback now. Rolling back will restore old modulus and prefetch mapping. Prep: run dry-run to confirm config available.

deploy-bot: rolling back prefix-hash to v2 initiated by oncall-joe. Action: config revert 9f4b2d3 -> 4a7c1b0. Starting staged rollback: 100% -> verify.

ops-bot: note: rolling back will generate high KV churn while caches warm. We should do aggressive warmup after rollback. Plan: 1) rollback 2) trigger warmup job for top-100 prefixes 3) monitor p95/p99 for 20 minutes

oncall-joe: warmup job queued: warmup-job-3162410100 targeting top-100 prefixes across shards.

maria-sre: running quick smoke after rollback applied:
```
post-rollback check @ 3162410200:
global: total_requests=76240 total_prefix_hits=68912 hitrate=90.4%
/v1/stream p99=1.12s p95=0.42s error-rate delta=+0.2%
```

sam-ml: looks like rollback recovered hitrate quickly, p99 improved but still above baseline p99 0.9s. Might be warmup finishing.

jess-product: should we notify customers that mitigation is in place and we're monitoring?

nate-cs: yes — sending note to affected TAMs: "Mitigation applied (rollback to v2). We show restored cache hitrate and improving latency. We'll monitor for 2 hours and follow up with root cause."

oncall-joe: tagging handoff to night: lina-oncall — I'll do a verbal/keyboard handoff. Critical next steps for night oncall:
- watch p99 for /v1/stream and global prefix hitrate (target >85%)
- verify warmup job completion and hit samples for hot prefixes
- escalate if p99 >1.6s for >10m or hitrate <70% for >15m
- coordinate with sam-ml for detailed postmortem (hashing logic review)

lina-oncall: ack, I'll take it. I'll keep an eye on the grafana panels and the warmup status. Please add the debug commands I should run.

oncall-joe: commands for quick checks:
```
# check prefix hitrate per shard
curl -s http://kv-monitor.internal/api/hitrate?since=10m | jq .shards

# top prefix miss sample
curl -s http://kv-monitor.internal/api/miss/sample?limit=20
```

lina-oncall: got it. Also will ensure the warmup-job logs show success across all AZs. Will open a short-running check on SLO alerting escalation if we cross the thresholds.

maria-sre: postmortem action items so far (draft):
- revert/modulus change rollback and add canary validation that checks hitrate delta on canary->50% step
- add a synthetic warmup/validation job pre-rollout that warms top-100 hot prefixes and verifies hitrate >=80% before 100% rollout
- add a safety cutoff in rollout pipeline if global hitrate drops >20% relative to baseline
- code-review hashing function for off-by-one and modulus boundary cases

sam-ml: agreed. I'll own the PR for adding canary hitrate checks and the synthetic warmup harness.

jess-product: product note: coordinate communication with affected customers: provide timeline of rollback and expected postmortem with root cause + mitigation steps.

oncall-joe: closing the live incident channel for now. Handoff completed to lina-oncall. I'll create an incident ticket (INC-2026-0315-001) and add logs/links. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup: 

lina-oncall: taking over monitoring. will update if anything regresses.

incident-bot: incident channel closed by oncall-joe at 2026-03-15T12:10:56Z."
